analysis:
Compared both composite actions' complete supplied BASE/HEAD source, patches and unchanged file modes. provider-ci-build/action.yml head lines 64, 91, 146, 154, 160 and 181 consistently disable Actions cache restore/save when CI_ACTIONS_CACHE is off; existing trusted-save conditions remain. Builds, timestamp revalidation, runtime-resource removal and Metal staging still run (103–142, 166–179). provider-release-build/action.yml head lines 120, 165, 185, 263, 275 and 392 apply the same gate without disabling source verification (72–80), Metal validation (171–183), qualification/audio tests (190–287), shard evidence or weak-import rejection (356–369). No supported regression in artifact integrity or qualification contracts (A-011, A-017, T-013, T-034, T-054), or availability (A-018), follows from these cache-only guards. No provider authorization, plaintext transport, billing, privileged-helper authority or inference prefix-cache behavior changes appear; T-041's runtime cache is distinct from these build caches.
Examined ci-master.yml metadata and bounded orientation patch: cache selection depends on RUNNER_NAME and DARKBLOOM_CACHE_URL and writes CI_ACTIONS_CACHE through GITHUB_ENV. Its remaining changes, including cached-.git sanitization and additional jobs, are not supplied as source units and the patch is truncated. Integration must inspect ci-master.yml changes around head 77–143 and 227–290 to establish cache-selection propagation before all cache steps and validate executable/configuration removal before using restored Git metadata. No finding is justified from absent code; this workflow coverage gap remains material to build integrity. Unchanged callers, helper implementations, runner isolation and cache-service routing were not examined.
